scenario: A regional bakery produces exactly six loaves — farmhouse, honey-oat, millet, pumpernickel, rye, and sourdough — in a single morning. The six loaves are distributed across two ovens, the North oven and the South oven, with each oven baking exactly three loaves. Within each oven, the three loaves are baked in a strict order: first, second, and third. The bakery's schedule is governed by the following conditions: honey-oat is baked in the North oven. Rye is baked third in its oven. Farmhouse is baked earlier in its oven than millet is in its oven (that is, farmhouse's slot number is lower than millet's slot number). Pumpernickel and sourdough are baked in different ovens. If millet is in the South oven, then honey-oat is baked first in the North oven.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be an accurate schedule for the bakery's morning production, listing for each oven the loaves baked first, second, and third, in that order?

choices.label: A
choices.text: North: farmhouse, honey-oat, millet; South: pumpernickel, sourdough, rye

choices.label: B
choices.text: North: honey-oat, sourdough, rye; South: farmhouse, pumpernickel, millet

choices.label: C
choices.text: North: honey-oat, pumpernickel, rye; South: sourdough, millet, farmhouse

choices.label: D
choices.text: North: millet, honey-oat, farmhouse; South: pumpernickel, sourdough, rye

choices.label: E
choices.text: North: sourdough, honey-oat, pumpernickel; South: farmhouse, millet, rye

explanations.correct: Choice A places honey-oat in the North oven, rye third in the South oven, farmhouse (slot 1) before millet (slot 3), and pumpernickel and sourdough in different ovens. All conditions are met, and because millet is in the North oven, the trigger for the conditional never fires.
explanations.A: Correct — honey-oat is in North; rye is third in South; farmhouse's slot (1) precedes millet's slot (3); pumpernickel and sourdough are split.
explanations.B: Pumpernickel and sourdough are both in the South oven, violating the different-oven rule.
explanations.C: Farmhouse is in slot 3 of the South oven while millet is in slot 2; farmhouse does not precede millet.
explanations.D: Rye is third in the South oven, but millet is in the North oven (South) triggering the conditional — actually the violation here is that farmhouse is in slot 3 of the North oven and millet is in slot 1 of the South oven, so farmhouse's slot (3) is not earlier than millet's slot (1).
explanations.E: Honey-oat is in the North oven and rye is third in the South oven, but millet is in the South oven, which triggers the conditional requirement that honey-oat be first in the North oven; here honey-oat is second.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Honey-oat is baked first in the North oven.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rye is baked in the South oven.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Farmhouse is baked first in its oven.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pumpernickel is baked in the South oven.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Millet is baked third in its oven.

explanations.correct: Honey-oat occupies one of the three North slots. Rye must be third in its oven. If rye were in the North oven, it would take North-3, leaving North-1 and North-2 for honey-oat and one other loaf. But pumpernickel must come after honey-oat in the same oven (honey-oat is North, so any loaf later in North must follow). Working through the numerical constraints — farmhouse must precede millet, and pumpernickel/sourdough must split — every valid world places rye in the South oven.
explanations.A: Not required. Honey-oat can be in North-2 when farmhouse is North-1, as in choice A of the orientation question.
explanations.B: Correct — rye cannot be accommodated as third in the North oven given the other placements required.
explanations.C: Not required. Farmhouse could be in slot 1 of the South oven with other arrangements.
explanations.D: Not required. Pumpernickel can be in the North oven with sourdough in the South.
explanations.E: Not required. Millet can be in slot 2 of an oven when another loaf occupies slot 3.

questions.questionStem: If pumpernickel is baked in the North oven, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Farmhouse is baked in the North oven.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sourdough is baked third in the South oven.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Millet is baked first in the South oven.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Honey-oat is baked second in the North oven.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rye is baked in the North oven.

explanations.correct: If pumpernickel is in the North oven, then sourdough is in the South oven. The North oven holds honey-oat, pumpernickel, and one more loaf; the South oven holds sourdough, rye (in slot 3), and one more. Farmhouse must precede millet, so millet is in the South oven and farmhouse is in the North oven. That triggers the conditional only if millet is in the South oven — which it is — forcing honey-oat to be first in the North oven. Wait: the conditional fires, so honey-oat must be first in North, meaning honey-oat cannot be second. Reconsidering: only choice that can hold is that sourdough is first or second in South and farmhouse arrangements work. Checking each choice against the forced placement (honey-oat North-1, rye South-3, millet in South): D is inconsistent with that forcing. The consistent choice is that sourdough is placed so that farmhouse's North slot number is less than millet's South slot number, which is always satisfied trivially across ovens only if we read 'earlier in its oven' — rereading rule 3, 'farmhouse's slot number is lower than millet's slot number' means the integer slot, regardless of oven. So farmhouse (North) slot < millet (South) slot. Farmhouse in North-1 (slot 1) and millet in South-2 or South-3 works. D: honey-oat North-2 — fails since conditional forces North-1. Thus the correct answer must be re-examined; under the intended reading honey-oat = North-1, pumpernickel = North-2 or North-3, farmhouse fills the other North slot. Sourdough third in South would bump rye — not allowed. Millet first in South means slot 1, but farmhouse in North is slot 1 as well — farmhouse's slot (1) is not less than millet's slot (1). So C fails. Rye in North contradicts rye being third with pumpernickel also in North. A is possible: farmhouse in North, consistent with honey-oat North-1, pumpernickel and farmhouse in North-2/North-3. The correct answer is A.
explanations.A: Correct — with pumpernickel in the North oven, the third North loaf must be farmhouse (honey-oat is forced to North-1, pumpernickel and farmhouse fill North-2 and North-3).
explanations.B: Rye must be third in its oven; if rye is in South, sourdough cannot be third in South.
explanations.C: Farmhouse would be in North-1 (slot 1) and millet in South-1 (slot 1); farmhouse's slot is not less than millet's, violating rule 3.
explanations.D: The conditional forces honey-oat to be first in the North oven whenever millet is in the South oven, which is the case here; honey-oat cannot be second.
explanations.E: Rye must be third in its oven, and pumpernickel must come after honey-oat in the same oven; placing rye in North with pumpernickel also in North leaves no slot for the required third North loaf consistent with farmhouse-before-millet across ovens.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Farmhouse is baked first in the North oven.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sourdough is baked second in the North oven.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Millet is baked third in the North oven.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pumpernickel is baked first in the South oven.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rye is baked third in the North oven.

explanations.correct: Rye must be third in its oven. If rye were third in the North oven, the North oven's three slots would be filled by honey-oat, rye, and one other loaf, with rye at slot 3. But honey-oat must precede pumpernickel in ordering, and farmhouse must precede millet. Together with the grouping constraints, no consistent assignment places rye in the North oven.
explanations.A: Possible — farmhouse North-1, honey-oat North-2, millet North-3 (with rye South-3) works.
explanations.B: Possible — honey-oat North-1, sourdough North-2, farmhouse North-3, with millet/pumpernickel/rye in South.
explanations.C: Possible — farmhouse North-1, honey-oat North-2, millet North-3 works.
explanations.D: Possible — pumpernickel South-1, sourdough South-2, rye South-3, with honey-oat/farmhouse/millet in North.
explanations.E: Correct — no valid world places rye third in the North oven.

questions.questionStem: If farmhouse is baked second in the South oven, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Honey-oat is baked first in the North oven.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Millet is baked in the North oven.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sourdough is baked in the North oven.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Pumpernickel is baked third in the North oven.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rye is baked first in the South oven.

explanations.correct: Farmhouse in South-2 means farmhouse's slot number is 2 (treating South as slots 4–6 or simply as slot 2 within its oven). Under the rubric reading that slot numbers refer to within-oven positions and 'earlier in its oven than millet is in its oven' requires farmhouse's within-oven slot < millet's within-oven slot, farmhouse at South-2 forces millet to be in the third slot of its oven. Since rye is already third in its oven, millet must be in a different oven from rye. With farmhouse in South, the South oven holds farmhouse plus two others; millet in slot 3 of the North oven satisfies the ordering. Hence millet is in the North oven.
explanations.A: Not required — honey-oat can be North-1 or North-2 depending on other placements.
explanations.B: Correct — with farmhouse South-2 and rye third in its oven, millet must be third in the North oven.
explanations.C: Not required — sourdough could be in either oven provided it differs from pumpernickel.
explanations.D: Not required — pumpernickel need not be third, and indeed if millet is North-3, pumpernickel is not North-3.
explanations.E: Not required — South-1 could be pumpernickel or sourdough; rye is South-3 if rye is in the South oven.
